title: Battery storage public meeting and new community grant policy
subtitle: Emergency management updates, permanent Community Connect program, draft Culture Action Plan, 2025 meeting schedule and Groves hospital board appointments.
overview: Council held a public meeting on a proposed zoning change and County Official Plan amendment for a battery energy storage facility at 6235 Guelph Street. No decision was made. Staff will report back and a by-law will come to a future meeting. One councillor recused from this item because of a family connection to the applicant's planning firm. A closed session was held earlier, and the Mayor said there was no report to bring forward.

Council adopted a new Community Investment Fund Policy to replace the Community Impact Grant Policy, and approved the 2025 annual specific grants. The new policy removes the capital grant stream, which a delegate from the Elora Centre for the Arts asked Council to keep. The Mayor stepped out of this item after declaring a conflict of interest.

Council also made the Community Connect program permanent and added the Fire Chief to the Emergency Management Programme Committee. It received the 2024 emergency management report and directed staff to seek public input on the draft Culture Action Plan through ConnectCW, with a final draft due in the first quarter of 2025. Council adopted the 2025 meeting schedule, appointed three Groves Memorial Community Hospital board members and removed a holding zone from the Centre Wellington Business Park lands in North Fergus.

decisions.detail: Council approved a by-law adopting the Community Investment Fund Policy in place of the Community Impact Grant Policy and approved the 2025 annual specific grants {{vote:m9}}.
Council received the pilot program update and approved creating a permanent Community Connect Program as outlined in the staff report {{vote:m8}}.
Council received the draft plan and directed staff to collect community input through ConnectCW and return in Q1 2025 with a final draft {{vote:m10}}.
Council updated the committee's composition to include the Fire Chief, who had been left off the original resolution {{vote:m7}}.
Council received and accepted the annual status report on the Township's Emergency Management Programme {{vote:m6}}.
Council adopted the 2025 schedule of Council and committee meetings and directed that it be posted on the Township website {{vote:m11}}.

decisions.item: Consent items: hospital board and business park zoning
decisions.detail: Council confirmed three Groves Memorial Community Hospital board appointments, approved removing the holding zone from North Fergus business park land, and approved rotating Deputy Mayor and committee appointment changes {{vote:m5}}.

debate: Residents and a local water-protection group raised concerns about fire risk, the large volume of water that might be needed, toxic fumes, groundwater and soil contamination, and reliance on a volunteer fire department. They asked for independent review, financial security from the operator, a smaller facility, or a declaration that the Township is not a willing host.

A farm organization delegate opposed the rezoning. The delegate said the project exceeds the size allowed for on-farm diversified uses on prime agricultural land, and that restoring compacted soil to farmland is very difficult. The delegate also raised concern about effects on municipal drains.

The applicant's team and fire consultant said the facility would use lithium iron phosphate batteries, sit well back from Second Line, and have a site-specific emergency plan developed with the local fire service. They said the applicant would cover firefighting and training costs, and that restoration to agriculture is feasible. The Fire Chief said the likely approach would be to protect nearby exposures rather than extinguish a fire.

Councillors asked what benefit the project brings to Centre Wellington, how noise was assessed given the planned South Fergus housing nearby, why the facility is the size it is, and what happens if the operator leaves. Staff noted that future road work on Second Line would be tied to development.

On the grant policy, the Elora Centre for the Arts delegate asked Council to keep capital funding and simplify eligibility rather than remove the stream. Staff said the stream takes significant staff time and few applicants qualify. Other programs could still fund smaller items.
